questions.question: Where should shipping papers be kept while driving?

options.text: Where you can easily reach them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can easily reach them.
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a door pouch or another location where you can reach them easily while wearing your seat belt. They must be visible to anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: When changing lanes, should you use your turn signal?

options.text: Only if another vehicle is close.

questions.explanation: Always signal before you turn or change lanes. Do not assume other drivers will move just because you are signaling.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, decrease your speed. Slowing down gives you more time to react to hazards.

questions.question: What should you do when leaving your vehicle?

options.text: Do not apply brakes if the vehicle is out of gear.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park. If needed, chock the wheels.

questions.question: What does a material's hazard class show?

options.text: How fast the material must be delivered.

questions.explanation: Materials are divided into nine hazard classes. Each class describes the specific dangers of that material.

questions.question: What do you need from a shipper to accept a package?
questions.explanation: The shipper certifies that hazardous materials are packaged correctly. You can accept this certification unless the package looks unsafe or breaks regulations.

questions.question: What is a Class 1 hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Class 1 includes explosives like ammunition, dynamite, and fireworks.

questions.question: When transporting explosives, what do you need?

options.text: You should take the shortest route.

questions.explanation: You must follow a written route plan for certain explosives. Avoid crowded areas, tunnels, narrow streets, and alleys. Check for any route restrictions.

questions.question: How can you avoid a hazard?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
You may need to swerve out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may need to swerve out of the way.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the best option. If you cannot stop in time, swerving may be your safest choice.

questions.question: A driver with their window open in cold weather may be:

options.text: A person who is dressed inappropriately.
A person who likes fresh air.

questions.explanation: An open window in cold weather can be a sign that a driver is impaired, drowsy, on drugs, or ill. Watch for this warning sign in other drivers.

questions.question: Trailers built before ____ do not need spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built before 1975 do not need spring brakes. When you park a trailer without spring brakes, use wheel chocks to keep it from rolling.

questions.question: What should you do if a hazardous materials label does not fit on the package?

options.text: Put the label on a tag and attach it securely to the item.
Attach a QR code that can be scanned.
Make the label smaller so it fits on the item.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the label on a tag and attach it securely to the item.
questions.explanation: Put the diamond-shaped hazard warning label on hazardous materials packages. If the label does not fit on the package, you can put it on a tag attached securely to the package instead.

questions.question: Smooth bore tanks have:

options.text: Bulkheads with holes that let liquids pass through.
Bulkheads that slow down liquid flow.
Nothing inside to slow down liquid flow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing inside to slow down liquid flow.
questions.explanation: Smooth bore tanks have no baffles inside. These tanks allow liquids to surge forward and backward more than other tank types.

questions.question: When you start a truck with a trailer, how can you tell the ABS is not working?

options.text: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
The red light on the right side of the trailer flashes three times.
All the rear lights flash and then turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
questions.explanation: When you start your engine, the dashboard lights should turn on and then turn off. If the ABS warning light stays on, the system is not working. For a truck with a trailer, if the yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on after starting the engine, the system is not working.

questions.question: A commercial motor vehicle driver:

options.text: Can use any cell phone while driving.
Can only use a hands-free cell phone while driving, if allowed.
Can only use a cell phone while driving on rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can only use a hands-free cell phone while driving, if allowed.
questions.explanation: If you use a cell phone while driving a commercial vehicle, use only a hands-free phone located close to you. Even hands-free phones can distract you. Know the cell phone laws in the state where you are driving.

questions.question: If you feel tired and yawn a lot while driving, you should:

options.text: Pull over and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop and get sleep. Do not try to keep driving to reach your destination while tired. Caffeine is not a reliable way to stay awake.

questions.question: Which is NOT a recommended way to spot vehicle problems?

options.text: Check critical items only at the start and end of a trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check critical items only at the start and end of a trip.
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle regularly during a trip to make sure it is working properly. Check the instrument panel, gauges, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights. Use all your senses and watch for anything that could be a sign of trouble.

questions.question: Pushing in the trailer air supply control will:
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull out the trailer air supply control to turn off the air supply and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: Bobtail tractors are ____ to stop than tractors with full semitrailers.
questions.explanation: Bobtail tractors are tractors with no semitrailer attached. When driving a bobtail, stopping is harder and takes longer than when driving a tractor with a loaded semitrailer.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should:
questions.explanation: If you meet an aggressive driver, do not react to angry gestures. Avoid making eye contact and do not try to race them.
